newsitem.title: FRANCE: Second ETBE plant starts production in France.
newsitem.headline: Second ETBE plant starts production in France.

text.p: West-ETBE, a new green-fuel plant built on the the site of a Total refinery in Gonfreville, Normandy, just started production, six weeks ahead of schedule, the French sugar beet federation (CGB) said on Monday.
The plant will produce 59,000 tonnes of ETBE (Ethyl-Tertio-Butyl-Ether) each year, an oil additive based on farm products, from 350,000 tonnes of ethanol, the statement said.
This is equivalent to 11,000 hectares of wheat and beet land. The total cost of the project stands at some 150 million francs.

West-ETBE is 40 percent held by Total, 40 percent by Ethanol Holding, a group of twelve partners in the grain and sugar industry, 10 percent by French wheat growers association AGPB and 10 percent by the CGB,
An ETBE plant of a similar capacity went on stream at the Total site of Dunkirk, in northern France, earlier this spring.
